newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Governors to oppose Clinton Medicaid plan-NYT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Governors to oppose Clinton Medicaid plan-NYT.

text.p: The United States' National Governors' Association plans to oppose President Bill Clinton's plan to set firm limits on federal Medicaid spending, the New York Times said on Friday.
The paper said a confidential draft of the group's new policy stated that any unilateral federal cap on Medicaid would unfairly burden the states with the cost of providing health care for the poor.
"The governors adamantly oppose a cap on federal Medicaid spending in any form," the paper quoted the draft as stating.
State and local governments pay 42 percent of all Medicaid costs, which totalled $67 billion out of $159 billion last year, the paper said.
Medicaid and welfare are expected to dominate the governors' winter conference, which begins in Washington, D.C., on Saturday.
Clinton is scheduled to present his budget next week.
